:::{#def-aic}
#### Akaike information criterion (AIC)

Let a model with $\nparams$ estimated parameters be fitted by [maximum likelihood](intro-MLEs.qmd#def-mle) to $\nobs$ observations,
and let $\llikf{\est{\vparam}}$ be the [log-likelihood](intro-MLEs.qmd#def-loglik) at the maximum likelihood estimate $\est{\vparam}$.
The **Akaike information criterion** of the model is

$$
\text{AIC} \eqdef -2 \llikf{\est{\vparam}} + 2 \nparams.
$$

It is minus twice the maximized log-likelihood, plus two for each estimated parameter.
For a Gaussian model, $\nparams$ includes the [noise](#def-noise) [variance](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/variance-covariance.html#def-variance).
A smaller AIC is better.

Source: @akaike1974new.
:::
